user.title: Haier HWHP – connection
user.description: Connection details for the Modbus TCP interface. The HWHP's native interface is Modbus RTU (9600 8N1), so the host is usually a Modbus RTU-to-TCP converter (gateway).

data_description.host: Usually the IP of the Modbus RTU-to-TCP converter, not the heat pump itself.
data_description.slave: Modbus address of the heat pump on the RTU bus (default 1).

cop.title: Haier HWHP – COP & energy
cop.description: COP = produced heat / electricity used. Leave a meter empty to use the device's integrated Modbus register; pick an entity to use an external meter. Tip: for an external electricity meter, pick a yearly-resetting counter (utility_meter, cycle: yearly) so the window matches the device's yearly heat total. Changeable later via "Configure".

data.cop_elec_entity: External electricity meter (kWh) — empty = Modbus register
data.cop_heat_entity: External heat meter (kWh) — empty = Modbus register
data.cop_ref_date: COP reference date (empty = auto; day the heat counter was reset)

pv.title: Haier HWHP – PV mode
pv.description: Optional PV-surplus control. Pick the operating mode: Off (only the raw entities + 38 °C guard), Coordinator (the integration controls setpoint and mode itself from PV surplus + a daily plan), or Executor (an external HEMS controls it via select.haier_hwhp_pv_program). The next page shows exactly the fields for the chosen mode. Changeable later via "Configure".

data_description.pv_mode: Off: the integration does not regulate (only the raw entities + 38 °C guard). Coordinator: the integration controls setpoint and mode from PV surplus — fixed morning start plus a surplus-driven cold start (together usually one run/day), raise to the elevated target only while the heat pump already runs (piggyback), plus Boost (heat pump + heater together) as a power sink above the boost threshold. Executor: an external HEMS controls it via the pv_program select; the integration only provides the programs.

pv_details.title: Haier HWHP – PV settings
pv_details.description: Settings for the selected PV mode. Coordinator: surplus sensor, target temps, daily plan and the control thresholds. Executor: only the target temps (the mechanic for the program select).

data_description.pv_sensor: Raw PV surplus in W (≥ 0). Required for Coordinator mode.
data_description.pv_temp_normal: Elevated target, must be reachable by the **compressor alone** — hence capped at 65 °C (data sheet: max. temperature output, heat pump only). Also the boost target: Boost is a power sink (heat pump + heater together), not its own temperature tier. Must be higher than the normal target temperature.
data_description.pv_temp_base: Normal target temperature (no surplus) — also the reference point for the night setback.
data_description.pv_temp_high: Only relevant for the Executor program now (select.haier_hwhp_pv_program, "Boost" program) — in Coordinator mode, Boost uses the same target as Elevated.
data_description.pv_hold: Buffer above which the heat-pump cycle is raised to and held at the elevated target — but the daytime raise happens only while the pump already runs (piggyback), so no extra cold starts. Drops back to normal after the debounce time once surplus stays below this and Boost is off.
data_description.pv_high: Boost threshold on the **normalized** surplus ("available" = raw surplus + heater power while Boost is running — makes the signal invariant to its own switching action). Must be at least the heater's rated power + 50 W, otherwise the heater would switch off into grid draw (auto-raised otherwise). Turning on debounces for the full time, turning off is immediate (one poll) — strict grid-draw avoidance.
data_description.pv_heater_power: Rated power of the electric heater per the data sheet (1500 W) — basis of the available-surplus normalization. No power meter required.
data_description.pv_power_entity: Optional: device total power (W), to derive the heater's power from the real measured step-up on switch-on instead of the rated value. Never a requirement — without an entity the rated value is used.
data_description.pv_morning_time: Once per day at this time, if the water is below the normal target, kick the setpoint to the elevated target so the heat pump starts within the device ECO window. Shares the daily quota (below) with the cold start.
data_description.pv_coldstart: Threshold (available surplus) above which — in addition to the fixed morning start — a cold start happens during the day if the water is below the elevated target. Debounces with the full debounce time, honours the same anti-short-cycle guard as the morning start and the same daily quota.
data_description.pv_coldstart_delta: How far below the raised target temperature the water must be before the surplus-driven cold start fires the heat pump. Prevents starts for a few degrees: the topmost degrees are the worst heat of the day (worst COP, highest standing loss). With a 65 °C target and 10 K, the cold start only fires below 55 °C. Smaller = more PV usage, larger = only substantial charges.
data_description.pv_abort_debounce: How long the surplus must stay below the hold threshold before an ALREADY RUNNING cycle is aborted. Deliberately much longer than the normal debounce: once the compressor runs, its start is already paid for — a passing cloud should not kill it, an actual sunset should.
data_description.pv_max_starts: How many ladder-triggered starts (morning start + cold start together) are allowed per day — default 1, for "as few compressor cycles as possible". Device-initiated starts don't count.
data_description.pv_min_off: Anti-short-cycle for EVERY setpoint raise while the pump is off (morning start AND cold start): waits until the compressor has been off at least this long. Daytime raises while already running (piggyback) are unaffected.
data_description.pv_escalation: What gets added once surplus passes the boost threshold. None: just the elevated target (the pump stays at max. 65 °C). Boost: heat pump + heater **together**, at the same target as Elevated — a pure power sink for substantial surplus, not its own temperature tier.
data_description.pv_boost_only_negative_price: If a negative-price sensor is selected (below) and this is checked, Boost fires **only** during the negative-price window. Without a selected sensor Boost then **never** fires — check the sensor is set first.
data_description.pv_negative_price_sensor: Optional binary_sensor/input_boolean flagging the current quarter-hour as negative/zero-price (e.g. your own template built on Tibber/aWATTar/Nordpool — this integration doesn't compute the price itself). **Only sensible with a dynamic tariff** — a negative exchange price cuts your feed-in revenue, not automatically your purchase price. When in doubt leave empty (default behaviour unchanged).

error.cannot_connect: Connection failed. Check host, port and slave ID.
error.pv_sensor_required: Please select a PV surplus sensor before enabling the control.
error.temp_order_normal: The elevated target temperature must be higher than the normal target temperature — otherwise there is no middle tier and the control tiers collapse.
error.temp_order_high: The boost target temperature must not be below the elevated target temperature.
error.pv_high_too_low: The boost threshold must be at least the heater's rated power + 50 W — otherwise the heater would switch off into grid draw.

abort.already_configured: This heat pump is already configured.

init.title: Settings (connection, COP, PV)
init.description: Connection, COP/energy sources and optional PV surplus control. Host/port/slave change the link to the Modbus converter.

data.cop_elec_entity: External electricity meter (kWh) — empty = Modbus register
data.cop_heat_entity: External heat meter (kWh) — empty = Modbus register
data.cop_ref_date: COP reference date (empty = auto; day the heat counter was reset)
data.legionella_interval_days: Interval – max. days without a full heat-up

data_description.pv_mode: Off: the integration does not regulate (only the raw entities + 38 °C guard). Coordinator: the integration controls setpoint and mode from PV surplus — fixed morning start plus a surplus-driven cold start (together usually one run/day), raise to the elevated target only while the heat pump already runs (piggyback), plus Boost (heat pump + heater together) as a power sink above the boost threshold. Executor: an external HEMS controls it via the pv_program select; the integration only provides the programs. The next page shows the fields for the chosen mode (skipped for Off).
data_description.emergency_enabled: When the water gets critically cold, temporarily switches ECO→AUTO/ELEC to heat immediately (even outside the ECO time window); back to ECO on recovery.
data_description.emergency_critical: Below this water temperature the emergency reheat escalates.
data_description.emergency_recover: At/above this water temperature it switches back to ECO.
data_description.emergency_mode: AUTO (default, previous behaviour): heat-pump priority, like a normal AUTO run. ELEC: heater only — fastest reheat, for when it's truly urgent. Reg 1 is a mode value (not a bitfield), so ELEC is a real mode switch, not a boost bit.
data_description.legionella_enabled: Forces a thermal disinfection at least every X days: heats the tank to the target until the bottom (tank bottom) holds the verification threshold for the hold time. If the tank gets fully heated anyway in between (e.g. PV boost), that counts and the timer resets. Scald risk: with 65 °C use a thermostatic mixing valve.
data_description.legionella_interval_days: A run is triggered after at most this many days without a verified full heat-up (DVGW practice: 7).
data_description.legionella_bottom_min: The run only counts as reached once the tank bottom – the coldest layer – holds this temperature (slightly below the setpoint).
data_description.legionella_hold_min: How long the tank bottom must hold the verification threshold before the run counts as successful.
data_description.legionella_window_start: Preferred time window (usually the device's ECO window): the run starts here if possible and first heats efficiently in ECO; if it can't reach the target it escalates to AUTO. When overdue, protection is forced even outside this window.
data_description.legionella_window_end: End of the preferred window (usually the device's ECO window).

missing_frontend_card.title: Missing Lovelace card: {card_name}
